memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites, 'If a man dies and leaves no son, give his inheritance to his daughter. If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers. If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father's brothers. If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, that he may possess it. This is to have the force of law for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses.'" - Num 27:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
From the case of five sisters, God establishes a lasting principle for all Israel. He lays out clear rules so that no family's inheritance would be lost when there was no son. Daughters, brothers, uncles, or the nearest relative would receive it in turn. What began as one family's need became a just law for the whole nation.

This shows how God cares about order and fairness in the life of His people. He did not want families cut off or inheritances lost through gaps in the law. So He provided clear guidance to protect the vulnerable and preserve what belonged to each family. God's laws often flow from His concern for justice and for those who might otherwise be forgotten.

There is beauty in how God responds to a genuine need. The sisters' faithful request did not just benefit them; it opened the way for many others in similar situations. When we act rightly and seek justice, the good often extends far beyond ourselves. God can use one faithful appeal to bless many.

Behind all these laws stands a God who is just and orderly, who cares for the weak and provides for His people. In Christ, we see this same heart perfectly displayed, a Saviour who ensures that none of His own are ever cut off from their inheritance (John 6:39). Trust the God whose justice protects and provides for all who are His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does God's care for order and fairness comfort you?
2. Have you seen God use one faithful act to bless many?
3. What does it mean that no one in Christ is cut off from their inheritance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Just and caring God, thank You that You provide for the vulnerable and protect what belongs to Your people. Help me to seek justice, trusting that in Christ none of Your own are ever lost. Amen.
